observations.source: Anglès Munné and Huber, SDP bounds on quantum codes: rational certificates
observations.read_scope: Definitions and normalization in Section2; Section3 introduction; full OpenProblem1 statement; Table1 and its caption/interpretation.
observations.confirmed: Table1 retains 2-3 for n7,d3 and 4-7 for n11,d4; unrestricted quantum subspace codes, not only stabilizers or CWS. A gap is source evidence, not proof of current openness.
observations.normalization_guard: Paper uses unnormalized A_j=sum|tr(E Pi)|^2 and B_j=sum tr(E Pi E† Pi); distance criterion is K*B_j=A_j. Do not mix with normalized enumerators.

replacement_lead.label: Open Problem1
replacement_lead.quote: The problem asks to provide a putative integer matrix weight enumerator
replacement_lead.exact_object: Integral matrix weights lambda_(i,j)^(t,p) obeying the stated symmetry-reduced SDP and additive constraints for hypothetical [[24,0,10]]_2, ordinary weights A10,A12,...,A24 = 18216,156492,1147608,3736557,6248088,4399164,1038312,32778 (plus A0=1).
replacement_lead.decision_value: A valid positive resolves matrix-moment feasibility only, not code existence. A sound necessary-constraint infeasibility certificate would exclude the hypothetical stabilizer code. Freshness, tractability and earlier equivalents not yet audited; sent to FreshPhysicsScreen.
